prompt: Complete ResourceRunner.useTwo so it opens two TrackedResources named "a" and "b" in a single try-with-resources statement; the tests verify that they close in reverse order (b, then a).
explanation: A try-with-resources statement can declare several resources separated by semicolons; each must implement AutoCloseable. When the try block finishes (normally or via an exception), the resources are closed automatically in REVERSE declaration order -- the last one opened is the first one closed. That mirrors how dependent resources usually need to shut down.
hints: The syntax is try (Res a = ...; Res b = ...) { ... } -- both declarations go inside the parentheses.
Construct each TrackedResource with the log and its name: new TrackedResource(log, "a").
You write no close() calls at all -- the compiler inserts them, closing b first because it was declared last.
